summary: Task grill of api-surface-trim across six ledgered Codex cold-read rounds. Rounds 1-2 corrected the contract shape (recordable criteria/contracts equality, the exact AppModule trim, PGHOST, test wiring, the D-0006 self-liquidation of config.ts). Round 3 raised a governance blocker — /health as fresh code owed §07/§05 compliance that 0012/D-0004 deferred; the human chose to BUILD the handler+logging, recorded as decision 0013. Rounds 4-5 worked through that decision's cascade (spec/plan/deferral reconciliation, the full §07 error payload, hermetic-vs-DB test reality) until the task had sprawled; the human chose to SPLIT observability into its own backend-observability task, returning api-surface-trim to a focused scope. Round 6's remaining items (Swagger's real route set, the AuthoredMeasureRegistry DB hook in onModuleInit, a 0013 wording inconsistency) are fixed or carried as implementation guidance in reviewer_focus. Stopped after round 6: the focused contract is well-specified and the residual depth is for the implementer + three-lens review, not further cold reads.
gaps: The exact AppModule trim was wrong: the plan claimed CoreModule provides auth/CSRF, but AuthGuard, LoginRateLimitService and the APP_GUARD CsrfGuard are declared in AppModule itself, and UsersController/GrantsController/UsageModule/HelpModule were omitted from the removal list
Acceptance criteria and plan_contracts were not in the exact equality the recorder requires
config.ts is on the .prettierignore D-0006 list, so editing it triggers the self-liquidating format-and-remove rule, which was outside the initial write scope
PGHOST also defaults to localhost and would resolve-trap; the initial contract only fixed frontendOrigin
The new tests were not wired into test:hermetic and the guard's pinned graph, so CI would never run them; the warehouse E2E command pointed at test:db, which excludes the oid test

/health is fresh code and owed constitution 07 (global exception handler) + 05 (structured logging) compliance that decisions 0012/D-0004 deferred — an impossible per-endpoint requirement without app-wide infrastructure
Bundling the handler+logging into api-surface-trim made it sprawl across governance, dependencies and testing, and forced a story re-approval

app.init() is not DB-free: AuthoredMeasureRegistry.onModuleInit queries Postgres, so route/swagger/health hermetic tests must stub it; the non-production Swagger surface is more than /api/docs + /api/docs-json; backend/test/ does not exist
contradictions: Decision 0012/D-0004 and the approved plan deferred the global handler+logging while the task built them — resolved by recording superseding decision 0013 (accepted), reconciling the spec, resolving D-0004 and re-deferring only DTO coverage as D-0009
Decision 0013's own Decision and Consequences named different owning tasks — made consistent on backend-observability
resolutions: The contract pins the exact AppModule shape (imports:[CoreModule,HealthModule], controllers:[AuthController], providers:[AuthGuard,LoginRateLimitService,APP_GUARD->CsrfGuard]) with the eleven removals enumerated
acceptance_criteria and plan_contracts are the same five strings
.prettierignore is in write scope and config.ts is formatted + removed from the D-0006 list in the same change
config.ts defaults PGHOST to 127.0.0.1 alongside frontendOrigin; main.ts binds 127.0.0.1 under AUTH_OTP_MOCK via an injectable listen seam; compose publishes both db ports to 127.0.0.1
The four DB-free hermetic tests join test:hermetic and the guard's pinned graph; the warehouse E2E is a WAREHOUSE_E2E=1-gated path in the already-hermetic oid test, not test:db

Human decision (2026-09-08): build the handler+logging — recorded as accepted decision 0013; then SPLIT them into a dedicated backend-observability task (after the frontend, before harness-wiring), returning api-surface-trim to a focused route-trim + security + warehouse + /health-success-DTO scope

Spec reconciled to 0013; approved plan left as-approved under 0013's supersession (decisions govern when plan prose drifts) to avoid a disproportionate story re-approval; D-0004 resolved and DTO coverage re-deferred as D-0009

Hermetic tests stub only AuthoredMeasureRegistry.onModuleInit before app.init(); the Swagger-absence test covers /api/docs, /api/docs/**, /api/docs-json, /api/docs-yaml; backend/test/ removed from write scope
open_items: NON-BLOCKING: stopped after six rounds. The focused contract is well-specified; residual round-6 depth (exact Swagger asset routes, config.ts production-secret refusal in the swagger test, the onModuleInit stub mechanics) is implementation guidance in reviewer_focus for the implementer + three-lens review, not a further cold read.

NON-BLOCKING: the approved plan's compliance note still reads 'deferred'; it is superseded by accepted decision 0013 and the reconciled spec. Re-editing the approved plan would force a story re-approval disproportionate to a note; decisions govern when plan prose drifts.
NON-BLOCKING: backend-observability is a thin appended task (10-task graph); its full contract is authored when it reaches the frontier, after the frontend.
current_flow: Today: AppModule registers Pulse's full capability set (routes reachable but broken after the trimmed migration); main.ts binds all interfaces; config.ts defaults to Vite's origin and localhost PGHOST; the warehouse oid test hand-builds SelectionExecutor; there is no /health, no global exception handler and no structured logging.

criteria_map.AppModule keeps exactly imports:[CoreMod: AppModule trimmed to imports:[CoreModule,HealthModule], controllers:[AuthController], providers:[AuthGuard,LoginRateLimitService,APP_GUARD->CsrfGuard]; the eleven capability registrations removed; proven by a route-registration test introspecting the initialized app (removed routes 404) and a production-Swagger-absence test over the full docs surface.
criteria_map.GET /health returns the standard respons: A HealthModule with a decorated success-envelope DTO ({success,data:{status:ok},error:null}) + example + typed @ApiOkResponse; proven by health.controller.test.ts asserting the runtime body AND generated schema. Runtime error handling is backend-observability's job (0013).
criteria_map.the backend mock-OTP profile is loopback: main.ts binds 127.0.0.1 under AUTH_OTP_MOCK via an injectable listen seam; config.ts defaults frontendOrigin->127.0.0.1:3000 and PGHOST->127.0.0.1; compose publishes both db ports to 127.0.0.1; config.ts formatted + removed from .prettierignore (D-0006). Proven by loopback-profile.test.ts asserting the defaults + compose bindings.
criteria_map.the warehouse E2E resolves WAREHOUSE and: The warehouse E2E resolves WAREHOUSE + SelectionExecutor from the app-module DI and returns 42 via a WAREHOUSE_E2E=1-gated path in the already-hermetic oid test (not test:db). Demonstrated host evidence.
criteria_map.hermetic DB-free tests (route allow-list: Four DB-free hermetic tests (route, swagger-production, loopback-profile, health) join test:hermetic + the guard's pinned graph, each stubbing AuthoredMeasureRegistry.onModuleInit before app.init(); login/RBAC/audit/no-enumeration/session-continuity stay demonstrated Postgres evidence (the real auth path needs a pool).

new_abstractions: A backend-observability task (split from api-surface-trim per the human) owning the global exception handler + structured logging — justified because bundling cross-cutting infrastructure into an API-surface trim made one task sprawl across governance, deps and testing.
A configureApp(app) seam + injectable listen seam so route/swagger/health tests exercise the real wiring via app.init() without binding a socket or adding a test dependency.

rounds.question: The grill flags that /health is fresh code, and decision 0012 says its deviation 'does not extend to any code written fresh' — so strictly /health owes a global exception handler and structured JSON logging with correlationId. But those are app-wide infrastructure (you can't have a global handler for just one endpoint), and they don't exist yet. How should api-surface-trim handle this?
options: Build the global handler + structured logging now
rounds.chosen: Build the global handler + structured logging now

rounds.question: Building the global exception handler + structured logging inside api-surface-trim has made it a large, sprawling task (5 grill rounds, and it now forces re-approving the whole story plan). How should we structure it?
options: Split observability into its own task (Recommended)
rounds.chosen: Split observability into its own task (Recommended)
